originalTitle: Morning Mail: Holes in Labor’s gambling law, IDF rejects criminal investigation into Frankcom death, Meta and child safety in spotlight
summary: Recovering addict says new laws will not prevent companies using inducements; Meta chief ‘misled’ regulators, whistleblower says
content: Good morning. Free booze, free footy and even free bets. These are the kinds of inducements used by gambling companies to keep addicts hooked, according to one recovering addict who says Labor’s reforms won’t stop the practice. The Israeli military has cleared itself over the 2024 airstrikes that hit a World Central Kitchen convoy, killing seven aid workers including Zomi Frankcom. Plus, our columnist Greg Jericho notes the disparity between falling real wages and plump corporate profits. Australia ‘Huge mistake’ | The former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios says he has made a “huge mistake” after being suspended from tennis after testing positive for cocaine while playing at an ATP event in Mallorca in June. Gambling bust | Labor’s gambling reforms have passed parliament but do not pass muster, according to the husband of the late Labor MP Peta Murphy. Plus, a recovering addict who was given $43,700 in betting inducements has “no confidence” that Labor’s crackdown “would have made my experience any different or any easier”. Roblox pledge | Roblox has committed to making changes to its online gaming platform after Australia’s eSafety commissioner discovered adults were still able to see child accounts and send connection requests without parental consent. Rent research | Critics of the government’s tax changes have latched on to research purporting to show that rents will rise up to 30%. But will they really? Luca Ittimani and Jonathan Barrett investigate. Exclusive | Almost one-fifth of older Australians who contested their Support at Home funding allocation determined by an algorithm had a higher level of support or higher priority allocated once a human reviewed the decision. World Mark Zuckerberg | A former Meta safety engineer has told a jury that the boss of the tech company, Mark Zuckerberg, “created a false and misleading impression of Facebook’s commitment to young people” and that the company was aware of the harm its products could cause children. IDF strikes | The Israeli military has decided not to open a criminal investigation into the 2024 strike on an aid convoy that killed Australian Zomi Frankcom and six others. But it admitted its troops had opened fire on a car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six family members in Gaza in 2024, and ordered a criminal investigation into that killing. Ukraine intrigue | Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has fired a senior aide amid a fresh corruption investigation – one day after a former defence minister warned the country was facing “a crisis of governance” and needed to hold a wartime presidential election. Progressives progress | Progressive Democrat Angie Nixon has upset the party establishment by winning won the US Senate primary in Florida, beating former army intelligence officer Alexander Vindman. Dog doubt | A British dog food brand has recalled all of its fresh meals after reports that a recipe change may have caused some animals to go blind. Full Story Decoding America: Why Maga vaccine scepticism might be catching Reged Ahmad and Jonathan Yerushalmy discuss what the USS Lincoln crisis says about whether the US military is stretched too thin as the war on Iran drags on. In-depth Greg Jericho has consistently argued that the RBA’s concerns about pay rises fuelling inflation are misplaced. In today’s column he highlights the crisis caused by the “pathetic” level of wage growth. Not the news Luke Buckmaster gives four stars to Sweet Milk Lake, the story of a trans man who return to who returns to his home town to see his terminally ill estranged father and in which Harvey Zielinski excels as director, writer and star of his feature debut. Sport Netball | The relaunch of a Super Netball club under the brand Sydney Sirens has been hailed by many fans as a source of celebration, energising the sport as it soars towards its Australian centenary in 2027 and a World Cup in the city. Cricket | England reached 112-2 at stumps on the first day of the First Test against Pakistan after Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each took five wickets to dismiss the visitors for 171. Football | Gianni Infantino has lost the support of another one of Fifa’s vice-presidents with the Hungarian federation chief criticising the president’s “professional judgment, ethical standards and leadership”. Media roundup The former Liberal staffer Fiona Brown has settled her claim against the commonwealth for $1.48m, the Australian reports. Concerns about roads, healthcare and crime are fuelling the surge in support for One Nation in regional Victoria, according to a poll in the Border Mail. A sacked Aldi shop assistant who used AI to generate a false unfair dismissal case has been hit with $1,230 costs for wasting the time of the Fair Work Commission, the Sydney Morning Herald reports. What’s happening today Environment | First Nations clean energy summit in Geelong. Inquiry | David Elliott due to appear at the NSW Icac hearing. Economy | ABS releases labour force data for July. chineseTitle: 早间邮报：工党赌博法存在漏洞，以色列国防军拒绝对 Frankcom 死亡事件进行刑事调查，Meta 和儿童安全成为焦点
chineseSummary: 正在康复的瘾君子表示，新法律不会阻止公司使用诱因；举报人称 Meta 负责人“误导”监管机构
chineseContent: 早上好。免费酒水、免费足球，甚至免费投注。一位正在康复的瘾君子表示，这些都是赌博公司用来让瘾君子上瘾的诱因，他表示工党的改革不会阻止这种行为。以色列军方已经澄清了 2024 年世界中央厨房车队的空袭事件，造成包括佐米·弗兰克科姆在内的 7 名援助人员死亡。此外，我们的专栏作家格雷格·杰里科（Greg Jericho）指出了实际工资下降与企业利润丰厚之间的差距。澳大利亚“巨大错误”|前温布尔登决赛选手尼克·克耶高斯 (Nick Kyrgios) 表示，他在 6 月份在马略卡岛参加 ATP 赛事时检测出可卡因呈阳性后被禁赛，他表示自己犯了一个“巨大的错误”。赌博半身像|已故工党议员皮塔·墨菲 (Peta Murphy) 的丈夫表示，工党的赌博改革已在议会获得通过，但尚未通过审核。另外，一名正在康复中的瘾君子获得了 43,700 美元的博彩奖励，他“不相信”工党的镇压“会让我的经历有所不同或变得更轻松”。 Roblox 承诺 |在澳大利亚电子安全专员发现成年人仍然能够在未经父母同意的情况下查看儿童帐户并发送连接请求后，Roblox 承诺对其在线游戏平台进行更改。租金研究 |政府税收改革的批评者关注了据称表明租金将上涨 30% 的研究。但他们真的会吗？卢卡·伊蒂马尼和乔纳森·巴雷特进行调查。独家|在对由算法确定的家庭支持资金分配提出异​​议的澳大利亚老年人中，近五分之一在人工审核决定后获得了更高级别的支持或更高的优先级。世界马克·扎克伯格 |一位前 Meta 安全工程师告诉陪审团，该公司的老板
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
